title: What they mean
objectives: Answer out loud: Explain EV vs. equity value without using a formula.
Answer out loud: Why do we need both?

steps.heading: Equity value
steps.body: the value of *all* of a company's assets, but only to common shareholders. Share price × diluted shares.

steps.heading: Enterprise value
steps.body: the value of the company's *core business operations* to *all* investors — equity, debt, preferred.
House analogy: a $500k house bought with $100k down and a $400k mortgage. The house (EV) is worth $500k. Your equity is $100k.
Current EV uses today's market price; implied EV comes from a valuation (DCF, comps).

blocks.template: Equity value = share price × {{1}} shares outstanding
EV represents the value of core operations to {{1}} investors
In the house example, EV = {{1}}, equity value = {{2}}

blocks.title: Why do we need both?
blocks.body:
Different questions, different investors. EV tells you what the business itself is worth regardless of how it's financed, so you can compare companies with different capital structures. Equity value tells shareholders what their stake is worth — it's what the share price reflects.

**Interview answer:** "EV lets you compare businesses regardless of financing; equity value tells shareholders what their piece is worth."

blocks.prompt: Why would you compare companies using enterprise value rather than equity value?

options.text: EV is always larger, so multiples are easier to read
EV is independent of how the business is financed
EV is what the share price reflects
EV excludes debt, which is volatile

blocks.explanation: EV captures the business itself regardless of capital structure, so companies with different debt levels are comparable.

blocks.title: Why is EV closer to the "real price" of a company?
blocks.teaser: An acquirer has to buy the equity and take on or repay the debt, while getting the cash.
blocks.body: An acquirer has to buy the equity *and* take on or repay the debt, while getting the cash. EV captures that total economic cost.

blocks.title: Book equity vs. market equity?
blocks.teaser: Book equity is an accounting figure from the balance sheet (historical cost).
blocks.body: Book equity is an accounting figure from the balance sheet (historical cost). Market equity value is what investors pay today. Valuation uses market values.
